accepted.question_text: Consider the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model (FA-1f) on Z, where each site updates only when at least one nearest neighbor is infected, and where the reversible equilibrium measure pi is the Bernoulli product measure with infected density q in (0,1). For any such q and any local observable f depending on finitely many sites, does the law of the process started from any initial distribution nu that almost surely contains at least one infected site satisfy lim_{t->infinity} |E_nu[f(eta(t))] - pi(f)| = 0?

evidence.quote: A second basic question is to determine under which conditions on q and on the initial distribution nu, the law of the process at time t converges to the equilibrium measure pi as t -> infinity.
Conjecture 1. For any q in (0, 1) and any function f depending on the state of finitely many vertices lim_{t->infinity} |E_nu(f(eta(t))) - pi(f)| = 0, provided that nu(exists an infected vertex) = 1.

accepted.question_text: In the one-dimensional FA-1f model on Z with infection density q > 0, suppose the initial distribution nu has exponentially decaying probability of containing no infected site in a symmetric interval around the origin, namely nu(no infected vertices in [-ell, ell]) = O(e^{-kappa ell}) for some kappa > 0. Under that assumption, is the convergence of the law at time t to the Bernoulli(q) equilibrium measure pi exponentially fast for every q > 0?

evidence.quote: The next obvious question concerns the speed of relaxation to the reversible measure pi under some condition on nu stronger than just the a.s. existence of some infection.

Conjecture 2. If there exists kappa > 0 such that nu(no infected vertices in [-ell, ell]) = O(e^{-kappa ell}) for all ell > 0 large enough then for all q > 0 the convergence in (1.1) is exponentially fast.

accepted.question_text: Let a kinetically constrained model have bootstrap-percolation stable configurations E, and for each beta in E let pi_beta denote the product Bernoulli equilibrium measure pi conditioned on the event that the bootstrap percolation limit BP(eta) equals beta. Must every stationary measure mu of the kinetically constrained model admit a decomposition mu = integral_E pi_beta dmu_star(beta) for some probability measure mu_star on E?

evidence.quote: In view of the discussion above and of Theorem 2.13, we propose the following conjecture.

Conjecture 3. Let mu be a stationary measure of a KCM. Then there exists a probability measure mu* on E such that mu = integral_E dmu*(beta) pi_beta, where pi_beta is given by the measure pi conditioned on the event {BP(eta) = beta}.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Finally, a related question in higher dimensions is the scaling with n of the mixing time of the ergodic chain on Lambda_n^d. The conjecture is a linear scaling for all values of q > 0, but, once more, that has been proved only for q large enough.

evidence.quote: Finally, a related question in higher dimensions is the scaling with n of the mixing time of the (ergodic) chain on Lambda_n^d. The conjecture is a linear scaling for all values of q > 0, but, once more, that has been proved only for q large enough [10].

needs_review.question_text_raw: In the finite-volume chain on Lambda_n one expects the cutoff phenomenon to occur for all q > 0, but the cutoff has been proven only for q not too small.

evidence.quote: In the latter setting, the mixing time of the chain scales linearly with n and one expects the cutoff phenomenon (see e.g. [14, Chapter 18]) to occur for all q > 0. The cutoff has been proven in [8] for q not too small.
